All three voters give SINGLE_SOURCE_OK / different_formulation; I confirm after reading pp. 101–102 and the Lean. Exponents match (good part α+1/2−3κ, pressure α+1/2), linearResidual matches (9.1)+(9.2), and excludedSlotError = (D_fast ψ)t + (1−ψ)f is exactly the paper's two tails. The full item is the conjunction of constructed_particular_wave(_with_flat_error), complexCopy_inputBounds and excludedSlotError_carrier_physical_bound, plus, for homogeneous pulses, the generic LinearWaveBounds theorem with pressure_class. I promote the generic theorem to co-'states' (PAIRING skeptic): the repo labels it the proposition (stale 'Proposition 9.3') and it alone covers f = 0. All six findings are low: attribution gaps or the class-encoding convention. Lean was not run; orphan status rests on grep.

findings.summary: Homogeneous-pulse case exists only through the generic theorem, which assumes π_m ∈ W_{α+1/2} (InputBounds.pressure) where the paper concludes it. The class is proved separately by pressure_class with f = 0.

The item's conclusions are spread over three declarations with the same hypotheses: with_flat_error omits the pressure class; constructed_particular_wave gives it only for the cut pressure ψπ_m; uncut π_m ∈ W_{α+1/2} is in complexCopy_inputBounds.

Headline flatness is chart-normalized (∀β, UnweightedClass β, with (S·max(1,δ⁻¹))^p growth allowed). The paper's Cartesian O(q^N) claim is a separate theorem with extra hypotheses (n ≥ 4, global source smoothness, phase-jet bounds, lift in domain).

WaveClass/MemClass records only smoothness and jet bounds on the open strip. Definition 6.5's support in Ω_γ, θ-independence and smooth zero extension are not part of the Lean conclusion for the residual.

Item-level theorems assume abstract control data (CopyControl energy/exponential bounds, Gaussian envelope hW = (7.16), ExactConditions on the output). They are not used by the main theorem; the modal form is reached only via LocalControl, never constructed.

Single-copy theorems fix one copy sequence copy : ℕ → Frequency and one label; constants are existential afterwards. Uniformity over copies and labels, required by the section convention, is stated only in the pipeline's UniformClass theorems.
